## 65a142eb4d9b

**Reproduced shortcut — normal lessons never exercise the isolation condition.** The canonical rule expands a colored singleton into a plus only when it has no same-color cardinal neighbor. The selected generator intentionally places unique, interior, widely separated colored cells, so an unconditional “stamp a plus around every nonzero cell” rival is indistinguishable on its normal domain.

Across 64 deterministic normal draws from generator SHA `9cb0848ff7ee131af330f07bed9ea29dfda0d1d8fc139270df877a7a6c315b27`, all 64 passed `self_check`, all 64 Racket applications succeeded under rule hash `7224a7556e4b`, and the unconditional rival matched the canonical output **64/64** times. I then constructed a 7×7 grid containing adjacent same-color `4` cells plus an isolated `6`. The weak validator accepts it; the canonical rule leaves the `4` pair unchanged and expands only the `6`, while the rival also expands the `4` pair, differing in six cells.

The counterexample is outside the generator’s stated normal-domain prose, so the primary finding is a curriculum/shortcut gap rather than proof that ordinary generated inputs violate their own declaration. Evidence: `checks/audit/65a142eb4d9b/summary.json`, `generated-inputs.json`, `generated-racket.json`, `generated-rival.json`, and the `counterexample-*` files. The target was not modified.
